text: So Paul went out from their midst.
display_text: So Paul went out from their midst.
deferral_reason: The local context gives mixed reactions before Paul goes out and believers afterward. It does not describe an expulsion or universal rejection. A separate generic departure adds no specific supported relationship to this brief exit notice.

text: They all seized Sosthenes, the synagogue ruler, and beat him before the tribunal. Gallio cared about none of these things.
display_text: They all seized Sosthenes, the synagogue ruler, and beat him before the tribunal. Gallio cared about none of these things.
deferral_reason: The local tribunal refusal and beating do not identify this Sosthenes with the brother named in 1 Corinthians 1:1, which supplies no matching beating or conversion history. The subject of 'they all' and Gallio's stated indifference must remain as printed; no named-person or generic judicial-indifference link is retained.

text: We crossed the open sea off Cilicia and Pamphylia and came to Myra in Lycia.
display_text: We crossed the open sea off Cilicia and Pamphylia and came to Myra in Lycia.
deferral_reason: The route through the sea off Cilicia and Pamphylia to Myra remains the specific information supplied. The nearby change of ship identifies the next stage but gives no independent or meaningfully comparative route for this leg; matching coastal names alone would add no supported relation.

text: We put in at Syracuse and stayed three days.
display_text: We put in at Syracuse and stayed three days.
deferral_reason: Syracuse and the three-day stay are the notice's only specific details. Another stop or a matching duration would not establish the same event or a meaningful shared action beyond ordinary travel, so the notice remains deferred.

text: of Matthat, of Levi, of Melchi, of Jannai, of Joseph,
display_text: of Matthat, of Levi, of Melchi, of Jannai, of Joseph,
deferral_reason: The Matthat-Levi-Melchi-Jannai-Joseph sequence is printed as this part of Luke's lineage. The nearby Matthew chain does not repeat it, and recurrent Levi or Joseph names do not establish identities or a missing genealogical bridge.

deferral_reason: Mattathias-Amos-Nahum-Esli-Naggai is an ancestral chain, with no stated offices or deeds identifying these men. Names Amos and Nahum alone do not identify the prophetic authors, and no matching ordered chain has been established.

display_text: of Maath, of Mattathias, of Semein, of Josech, of Joda,

text: of Melchi, of Addi, of Cosam, of Elmadam, of Er,
display_text: of Melchi, of Addi, of Cosam, of Elmadam, of Er,
deferral_reason: Melchi-Addi-Cosam-Elmadam-Er remains a distinct printed lineage segment. Repeated names elsewhere do not reproduce these ordered relationships or authorize an identity for an individual ancestor.

text: of Jesus, of Eliezer, of Jorim, of Matthat, of Levi,
display_text: of Jesus, of Eliezer, of Jorim, of Matthat, of Levi,
deferral_reason: The ancestor named Jesus is followed by Eliezer-Jorim-Matthat-Levi in the printed chain. His name does not identify him with Jesus Christ or permit replacement by another form of the name; the repeated Matthat and Levi names do not establish a matching external chain.

display_text: of Simeon, of Judah, of Joseph, of Jonam, of Eliakim,
deferral_reason: Simeon-Judah-Joseph-Jonam-Eliakim is the actual ordered segment. Familiar patriarchal or royal names alone do not identify these ancestors, and the reread Matthew sequence does not supply the same relationships.

display_text: Azor begot Zadok; Zadok begot Achim; Achim begot Eliud;

text: Eliud begot Eleazar; Eleazar begot Matthan; Matthan begot Jacob;
display_text: Eliud begot Eleazar; Eleazar begot Matthan; Matthan begot Jacob;
deferral_reason: The Eliud-Eleazar-Matthan-Jacob chain remains distinct from Luke's printed nearby lineage. Matthan cannot simply be identified with Matthat, and the different Joseph-parent notices cannot be reconciled by inserting an unstated relationship. No matching sequence is retained.

text: Greet Ampliatus, my beloved in the Lord.
display_text: Greet Ampliatus, my beloved in the Lord.
deferral_reason: Ampliatus is greeted as beloved in the Lord, with no stated second episode, task or family connection. A similarly affectionate salutation is too broad to add a specific supported relationship to this person.

text: Greet Apelles, approved in Christ. Greet those of Aristobulus’s household.
display_text: Greet Apelles, approved in Christ. Greet those of Aristobulus’s household.
deferral_reason: The notice distinguishes Apelles's approval in Christ from the greeting to those of Aristobulus's household. Other household salutations, including 2 Timothy 4:19, do not identify these people or add a concrete shared act; approval alone supplies no stated biography.

text: Greet Herodion my kinsman. Greet those of Narcissus’s household who are in the Lord.
display_text: Greet Herodion my kinsman. Greet those of Narcissus’s household who are in the Lord.
deferral_reason: Herodion's kinsman description and the qualification that the greeted members of Narcissus's household are in the Lord must remain distinct. Another household greeting neither identifies Narcissus nor establishes the condition of every member of his household.

text: Greet Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine.
display_text: Greet Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine.
deferral_reason: Mark 15:21 names a Rufus as Simon's son but does not identify him with this greeted man or name the mother mentioned here. The mother-language of 1 Timothy 5:1-2 supplies a general relational instruction rather than this woman's identity or the precise sense of 'and mine'; no specific pair is retained.

text: Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers with them.
display_text: Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers with them.
deferral_reason: The five named men and the brothers with them form the stated greeting group. The text supplies no common task or second identified episode for them, and shared names or a similar group-salutation frame do not establish one.

text: Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas and all the saints with them.
display_text: Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas and all the saints with them.
deferral_reason: Philologus, Julia, Nereus with his sister, Olympas and the saints with them remain the named greeting group. The notice does not assign spouses, offices or a house location; another list of greeted saints would add only the generic salutation pattern.
